meta.bron_grondtekst: Westcott-Hort Greek New Testament with Strong-G tagging
meta.methodiek: Pure linguistic concordant translation. For each Strong-number a single concordant English rendering is chosen on the basis of seven anchors: (1) the consonantal root and its core meaning, (2) the morphology (form, case, number, person, gender, verb tense-mood-aspect), (3) the stem-family (related Strong-numbers), (4) cognates in related languages (Hebrew Septuagint counterpart, classical Greek, Latin) where relevant, (5) the Septuagint as a linguistic witness (not as authority) - especially relevant for Greek Strongs where the NT builds on LXX-meaning, (6) the word-formation (prefixes, suffixes, compounds, derived forms), (7) distribution across the entire Scripture: the word is checked in all occurrences (Mt-Rev) and the common-denominator meaning is identified through context-analysis of each occurrence. No tradition-preference, no theology, no school-choice. Existing English translation traditions (KJV, NIV, ESV, NASB, RSV, NRSV, NET, etc.) are admissible only as external reference, never as authority for the concordant choice.
